answer: A defense is attestation-bound identity. Each agent registers a hardware key a secure chip issues once; the registry grants one identity and a fixed work quota per key. A thousand fake agents therefore need a thousand attested chips plus hosting, a bill scaling linearly and impossible to pool. Reputation and a slashable bond stay bound to the key, so each clone holds zero history and real collateral. In a gale of automated signups quotas throttle volume before fraud spreads, trust bends willow-like without breaking, and each retired key leaves an umber trace that blocks silent re-registration.
